about: ResourceDownload — a file a reader can take away: a report, a slide deck, a recording. Its title is the link, and under it what the reader is about to get: the format, the size and how long it is. Use

title.about: What the file is, as a title ("Annual report 2026"). It is the link's text.

format.about: The file's format as a reader knows it: "PDF", "Excel", "PowerPoint", "CSV", "MP3".

size.about: How big it is, as it should read: "1.2 MB". Worth giving: it tells a reader on a phone what they are in for.

length.about: How long it is, as it should read: "24 pages", "18 slides", "32 minutes".

date.about: When it was published, as an ISO date. Goes in the time element's datetime.

dateLabel.about: The date in words, when the formatted one is not what you want.

description.about: One or two sentences on what is in it.

download.about: Ask the browser to save the file rather than open it. Leave off for PDFs, which most readers want to open.

alternativeHref.about: Where to ask for the file in another format, when it may not suit assistive technology.

headingLevel.about: The level of the title's heading, to fit the outline of the page it is on.

locale.about: The locale the date is written in.
